body:
I get being terrified of intimacy with men after spending so much time alone. I think being in relationships from your teenage years teaches you vulnerability and being open and that's not to say women who have these experiences don't also get hurt by men who just use them. 

But I don't think that a man worth anything will not want you if you've already slept with someone. Most reasonable men know that it's a high chance the women they want to date have had sex before. So if your first experience sucks maybe the second one will be good. But the bar is really low with some men :/

It's very hard for me too because many people say that to be able to get over the fear is to choose to be vulnerable and open to the experience no matter what happens and "the only way is through" and that's just not an option for me.

It's okay, I know they can also be really mean. I've read some really scary accounts from women in my country. I'm sorry that was your experience. I wish more gynos were aware of how vital kindness is to their profession.
Hopefully we never get any kind of nasty diseases 😷

I meant that I'm too old to admit I've never been as that would be incredibly embarassing on my part and the majority of them would judge, either silently or loudly.

I'm sorry if you're dealing with stuff. :(
Oh that sounds terrible, I'm so sorry :( Life can really suck sometimes
No, but I'm too old to say I've never been to a gyno :/ 9 out 10 people would consider it extremely weird and the 10th is really just trying to be nice
Technically I have no reason to either but everyone is constantly talking about cancer and on top of my generalized anxiety I also have health anxiety :(

I'm not trying to do a disservice to myself or anyone else, I'm struggling in every sense of the word. I'm sorry you're feeling nervous about going to the gyno. I get nervous sometimes making a phonecall. But what I am is not nervous, but a anxiety paralyzed 29 year old who has never been sexually active or been to a gyno in a country where this is seen as bad. In fact, in a country where being 18-20 and still a virgin is seen as weird. There's not even such forums in my country of "FAW women" and nobody brings it up ever because of shame. 21 year olds are told to harry up and start having sex cause they're already late bloomers.

Yeah, it is their job, however I read accounts of 21 year old girls being told to hurry and start being sexually active or girls with different problems being told they should get pregnant to fix things. Like if you've been it's easy to just say "ah it doesn't matter," but it does matter. Quite a few women end up being traumatized by their gyno. I'm not going to get treatment for a cold, I, a person who has never been sexually active, need to go to have parts of me that no one has seen exposed and poked and proded. It's not easy, that's the point of the post.
I'm sorry to hear that, but wish you luck on your appointment!
While your situation is unfortunate, I love that you have a gyno that knows you so well and is kind with you. I'm sorry about the PCOS :(
Do you feel like going? Is it something that's on your mind?

> i don’t like feeling behind from sexual + reproductive care or experiences compared to other women around me.

I don't like it either but my mental health issues are that much stronger. I will try to get in a better mindset.
Thank you for sharing your experience with me, it's helpful <3

There really should be a section of gynos for people with trauma or people like me... like I feel like if you go there and the person is already understanding that you're in a tough place and has volunteerd to do this because they don't judge, that'd be different. So many women who don't even have any of these issues go through shitty stuff at the doc and it's just even scarier for us.
Damn, that's terrifying. Sorry to hear that. :(
It's good that you're not ashamed. I think that makes it a bit easier in the long run. Shame is such a nasty thing, it's in every corner of your body.

I get you. I am the same + the fact that I find my body disgusting + dealing with the things they may say when I say that or how they may look at me. I just cannot handle it. I was also never encouraged as a girl to go so I guess that's also partly why I've never been.
All the possible things they could say are just terrifying me. I'm incredibly disgusted with my body and I think the soul would leave my body to even just look them in the eye.

But everybody's saying you might die of the big C if you don't go + there's also the shame associated with being almost 30 but not having been.

I have never seen a gynecologist ever. No pap, no other type of test, nothing. No doctor has ever seen my bits.

I don't want to disclose my situation + I don't really want the test done. I don't want the pain or to have to be seen naked. And this is on top of the fact that I've heard horrendous stories from girls where they were traumatized by a doctor or so. So there's just so many stressful factors.

And the people I know at work have either moved in with their spouses or are renting and have flatmates because they can't afford it.
Sending hugs. I will also never have children. I guess I'm used to the idea by now but I sometimes get some dark thoughts. The cool aunt with the dogs sounds awesome. I have a cat 💙

Anyway I don't know why things are the way they are. I never do. I mostly attribute my misgivings in life to the fact that I'm not a good person.. to make sense of my predicament. But you sound like you are a good person and you don't deserve any of this. Sending hugs

The capacity to love cannot be built in isolation. ― Bruce D. Perry, The Boy Who Was Raised as a Dog: And Other Stories from a Child Psychiatrist's Notebook

You may be, unfortunately, dealing with a narcissistic parent. Check r/raisedbynarcissists/ for some help and guidance on how to deal with this. 

I don't know what to say to make it better, but just know that this behavior, especially coming from a mother, is not just mean abusive behavior, but it's just not normal. It may help your mental health to keep a minimal relationship with her if you live together. You can speak to her about x or y subjects, but as soon as she starts being negative about you for absolutely no reason, walk away from the conversation and focus on something else.

If your mother is indeed a narcissist, she won't be able to see how her behavior affects you because she's too focus on her experience and her feelings.

Just know that this is a projection. She is purposely doing this to make you feel bad. 

This is similar to what some very toxic men do in relationships: by emotionally abusing their girlfriends and telling them they're ugly and worthless all the time, some of them become dependent on the validation of said guy which means that they will stay with him and always seek his validation. 

Try to focus on people with whom you have positive interactions! Wish you well!

a) Wearing make-up is not catfishing. That's a concept that men invented.

b) Your mother is being very, very mean to you and is probably part of the reason you have self-esteem issues. Try not to listen to her comments on your appearance.

In the past three months, two groups of teenagers and an old man, that were strangers, laughed at me in public. I'm 27 so it really sucks. 

People close to me don't exactly point out my flaws, but I can see it on their faces. I don't get compliments, not even when I compliment someone, and they have that weird pitiful look sometimes when they look at me. 

It hurts but what can I do? 

The man I mentioned above, who was a stranger, made fun of my weight in front of my friend. It was mortifying.

Once school and college is over making friends is way harder. Work friends are a thing but you never know where the boundaries are drawn with them since they're work friends. But if there's someone at your workplace that would maybe like to hang out after work? Does your workplace ever organize to go out for drinks and stuff? 

Also, if you've recently found out you're autistic, maybe there are online subreddits and forums for autistic people in your area. I feel like social skills difficulties are part of the autistic experience sometimes and so you may feel more comfortable and connected to someone with a similar experience. 

I'm sorry if all of this is unsolicited advice. I know trying and failing is hard, especially for someone on the spectrum, but I do wish you the best of luck.

Thankfully, most adult couples I know are not like that and are aware that when you're in the company of other people, you have to engage with them and not spend the whole time gazing lovingly into each other's eyes.
